gmail_api.dependencies: Optional requirements/gmail.txt installed into .venv by launchers/Connect Jarvis Gmail API.cmd; google.auth and google_auth_oauthlib are loaded only during account setup/use.
gmail_api.credentials: Desktop OAuth client JSON stays at user's local path; tokens encrypted using Windows DPAPI in ignored .jarvis-runtime/gmail-api/token.dpapi; no cookies or account passwords.
gmail_api.lifecycle: Explicit interactive OAuth loopback listener for at most 300 seconds; closes after consent. Per-call HTTP session closes in finally, bounded requests, no automatic mailbox write retry.
gmail_api.activation: Local OAuth profile check and current gmail_api.py source hash; actual account consent, approved recipient-free draft create/update/readback and search/read passed on 2026-10-09. Reviewed source changes require explicit reconnection or --verify-existing profile check with encrypted credentials; no automatic credential or write replay.
gmail_api.operations: Direct API domain workflows for search/list, selected message text reads, draft read/create/update; literal commands bypass inference, natural composition uses scoped text-only Qwen. Official draft query filtering, unchanged MIME/field preservation, expected raw hash, exact readback and durable uncertain-write journal. Sending, deletion and file attachment downloads are not exposed.

utility_skills.lifecycle: Owned local preview in Actions.utility_server is closed by Actions.close; no always-running new daemon; no shared process termination or uncertain mutation replay.

User loads it into existing logged-in Chrome. Owned UI worker binds authenticated 127.0.0.1:29923 only for its lifetime; bounded one-lease requests and current-source handshake. Compose/optional To/Subject/body drafts only, no filesystem folder, sending/attachments/inbox reading disabled. Live draft proof required before activation.
utility_skills.verification: artifacts/reports/utility-validation.json distinguishes actual local tests and external-service mock contracts; docs/utility-skills.md records unresolved live checks. No blanket production-readiness claim.

gpu_scheduler.lifecycle: No extra server/process; atomic local state with short OS lock, PID creation-time ownership, bounded queue and cancellation/dead-owner cleanup
gpu_scheduler.health: Metadata-only gpu status in existing operational heartbeat; admission/handoff/dispatch/release events under .jarvis-runtime/gpu
gpu_scheduler.memory: Conservative partial-layer envelope, 1024 MiB speech floor and 512 MiB additional headroom; actual external usage read from nvidia-smi
gpu_scheduler.cache: Same primary model uses 16384-token context and a 30-second warm cache; different-model handoff unloads only a freshly matched owned cache once
gpu_scheduler.coding: Local Codex Responses model alias: 9 GPU layers, 32768-token context; preserved tool protocol and no CLI/global-home changes; observed successful coding cache gets a 30-second timer and identity-checked handoff
gpu_scheduler.coding_completion: Finalize inference lease/cache before forwarding terminal Responses completion, so Codex job shutdown cannot orphan bookkeeping; retain observed cache identity if its timer update is unconfirmed
gpu_scheduler.limits: Nonpreemptive current inference; external GPU clients are not scheduled or killed. Native low-memory inference falls back to CPU; coding refuses before inference if its reserved alias footprint cannot fit. Helpers default to CPU after measured cold-start comparison; optional helper_gpu only admits idle GPU work.
gpu_scheduler.recovery: Existing owned worker shutdown; abandoned leases reaped by PID birth identity, no task/action replay; corrupt state fails closed and is preserved

fast_planning.configuration: gpu_scheduler.warm_seconds and cpu_threads; brain.planner_images (auto|always|never), brain.fused_verification, brain.max_recoveries
fast_planning.inference: Primary model stays loaded for warm_seconds and uses cpu_threads for its CPU layers; each task's next-step calls form one growing conversation so the hybrid model reuses its cache (measured prompt reading 1.2-5.5 s instead of 18-24 s)
fast_planning.screenshots: Sent to the planner only for recovery, unconfirmed outcomes or windows with fewer than six readable controls; planner copies are downscaled to 1024 px
fast_planning.verification: Incremental tasks check the window change and let the next planning call judge the outcome; navigation and read-only tools skip the extra decision call; the planner's finish after a confirmed step is the goal check
fast_planning.recovery: Navigation/click failures are re-planned from fresh observation up to max_recoveries (default 5); a failed or completed action is never repeated; uncertain writes (files, commands, typing, closing apps, approval tools) still pause
fast_planning.lifecycle: No new process or service; no automatic replay of any action

conversation_and_queue.configuration: wake_timeout_seconds (call-mode listening window, default 600); suggestion_seconds (UI suggestions, default 90); context_selector.model for chat-vs-task classification
conversation_and_queue.queue: New requests wait behind running work with a spoken acknowledgement; per-task cancel tokens; cancel this task / stop all tasks / what's in the queue
conversation_and_queue.conversation: Ending a conversation (goodbye, go to sleep) stops listening without cancelling queued tasks; unrecognised speech is classified as chat or task by rules then qwen3.5:0.8b on CPU; small talk never triggers web search; saved-conversation choices only for explicit references to the past
conversation_and_queue.lifecycle: Uses the existing action and knowledge workers; the classifier runs on a short daemon thread per unrecognised utterance
